title: rucc corpus report, version 1
description: The machine readable summary of one corpus run. Written to reports/report.json. The schema version is in the report itself, in the schema field, and it is a string rather than a number so that a version can be a date if it ever needs to be. A field is added without a version bump. A field is removed or changes meaning only with one.

schema.description: The version of this schema the report was written against.

milestone.description: Which milestone of the compiler plan the corpus is written for.

tool.description: What wrote the report, with its version.

corpus_digest.description: SHA-256 over every case in the corpus. Two reports with different digests are about different programs, and comparing their numbers directly is a mistake. This is what rucc-corpus diff checks before it says anything.

cases.description: How many programs are in the corpus.

reference.description: The id of the toolchain the others are measured against.

levels.description: The optimization levels that were built.

totals.description: One entry per toolchain, counting every build it did across every level.

targets.description: The falsifiable claims the compiler plan makes, and whether this run met them.

findings.description: Every result that was not what the generator said it would be. Empty is the good case.

id.description: What it is called in every other part of this report. Chosen by whoever ran it, so that a report from a laptop and a report from CI line up even though the binary was in a different place.

version.description: The first line it printed for --version.

reference.description: Whether the others are measured against it.

tally.description: How a set of builds came out. Every build lands in exactly one of the seven verdicts, so pass through crashed sum to ran and skipped is the rest.

pass.description: Did what the generator said it would.

wrong.description: Compiled, ran, printed something else. The worst kind.

rejected.description: Refused a program that is valid C.

unimplemented.description: Refused a program that is valid C, having said itself that the construct is not built yet. Counted and reported, and not a failure.

accepted.description: Accepted a program that is not valid C, or rejected it for the wrong reason.

crashed.description: Fell over, timed out, or died on a signal.

skipped.description: Not built, because the case asked to be left out.

failures.description: Everything that is a bug, so wrong plus rejected plus accepted plus crashed. Not unimplemented, which is a gap the compiler declared, and not skipped.

pass_rate.description: Passes over ran, or zero when nothing ran.

compared.description: How many cases had a number on both sides, so the ratios below are medians over this many.

size_ratio.description: Median of this toolchain's executable section bytes over the reference's, at -O2. One is level with the reference and more than one is bigger.

speed_ratio.description: Median of this toolchain's run time over the reference's. Less than one is faster.

compile_ratio.description: Median of this toolchain's compile time over the reference's. Less than one is faster to compile.

ratio.description: A median ratio against the reference, or null when neither side produced a number. Never one as a stand-in for missing, because a missing measurement and a measurement that came out level are different facts. Medians rather than means throughout, because the corpus is full of tiny programs where one instruction is twenty percent.

target.description: One claim from the compiler plan, checked.

threshold.description: The number the claim has to beat.

facet.description: One named transformation, and how every toolchain did on the programs written for it.

describes.description: What the facet is about, in one sentence.

reference_said.description: What the reference compiler reported through -fopt-info on these programs. Reference data and not a pass or fail signal. A high missed count means the transformation was available and the reference did not take it, which is a hint about the program rather than about anybody's compiler.

finding.description: One build that did not come out as the generator said it would.

case.description: The case id, which is also the file name under programs.

summary.description: The finding in one line, for a list.

expected.description: What it should have printed, or the diagnostic it should have produced.

actual.description: What it printed, or what the compiler said.
